title: Preparation and extraction of chorion proteins from Salmo salar embryos for SDS-PAGE
author: Pérez-Atehortúa, Short, et al.

steps.title: Wash chorion samples
steps.instruction: Rinse each chorion sample sequentially with Wash solution 1 then Wash solution 2, discarding the supernatant after each wash.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Wash solution 1 (pH 8.5) containing 100 mM EDTA, 500 mM NaCl and 1 µL protease‑inhibitor per 100 mL.
Prepare Wash solution 2 (pH 8.5) containing 500 mM NaCl and 1 µL protease‑inhibitor per 100 mL.
Immerse samples in Wash solution 1, gently agitate, then discard the liquid.
Immerse the same samples in Wash solution 2, gently agitate, then discard the liquid.

steps.title: Check sterility (optional)
steps.instruction: Take aliquots of supernatant and chorion after each wash for microbial culture.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate PDA medium for fungal culture and LB medium for bacterial culture.
Incubate and observe daily for 7 days to confirm absence of growth.

steps.title: Discard final wash liquid
steps.instruction: After the second wash, remove and discard the remaining H₂O supernatant.

steps.title: Weigh chorion for extraction
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.05–0.08 g of washed chorion (in triplicate) into a 7 mL Pico‑Glass vial.

steps.title: Add SDS extraction solution
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of SDS extraction solution (Tris‑HCl 100 mM, Urea 8 M, 1 % SDS, β‑mercaptoethanol 300 mM, EGTA 10 mM, 1 % protease‑inhibitor cocktail) to each vial.

steps.title: Heat and homogenize
steps.instruction: Extract proteins by heating and mechanical disruption.

substeps.instruction: Place vials in a 75 °C water bath for 15 min.
Homogenize each sample with an IKA™ ULTRA‑TURRAX™ T 18 digital disperser for 20 s, washing the disperser tip between samples.
Return vials to the 75 °C water bath for an additional 5 min.
Homogenize again for a brief second pulse (as previously described).

steps.title: Clarify extracts by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenates to separate soluble proteins.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 1 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the clear supernatant to a labeled Eppendorf tube.
Store the supernatant at –20 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Precipitate SDS‑extracted proteins
steps.instruction: Perform protein precipitation on supernatants obtained with the SDS extraction solution (procedure illustrated in Fig 6).

steps.title: Quantify protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein amount using the Bradford assay (compatible with BL and U8M extracts; SDS extracts must be precipitated first).

steps.title: Store extracted proteins
steps.instruction: Keep all extracted (and, if applicable, resuspended) protein samples at –20 °C until electrophoresis.

steps.title: Prepare SDS‑PAGE gels
steps.instruction: Cast separating and concentrating gels according to the listed compositions.

substeps.instruction: Clean the glass plates with ethanol and let dry.
Separating gel (12 % acrylamide, total 10 mL): mix 2.5 mL Buffer lower, 4.08 mL A/BA, 3.25 mL H₂O, 100 µL 10 % SDS, 150 µL APS, 20 µL TEMED. Pour into the plate leaving 1–2 cm from the top.
Add a few drops of isopropanol on the surface, allow polymerization, then remove the isopropanol.
Concentrating gel (4 % acrylamide, total 5 mL): mix 1.25 mL Buffer upper, 0.65 mL A/BA, 3.05 mL H₂O, 50 µL 10 % SDS, 60 µL APS, 20 µL TEMED. Pour over the separating gel to overflow.
Insert a 15‑well comb (1 mm spacing, 26 µL well volume) and let the gel polymerize completely.

steps.title: Prepare samples for loading
steps.instruction: Denature and aliquot protein samples for electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: After precipitation and resuspension in H₂O, take an aliquot containing exactly 3 µg protein.
Add 5X loading buffer (62.5 mM Tris‑HCl pH 6.8, 2 % SDS, 10 % glycerol, 0.01 % bromophenol blue) to reach a final volume ≤20 µL (i.e., dilute to 1X).
Denature at 95 °C in a block heater for 10 min, then place on ice for 1 min.
Centrifuge the tube in a MiniSpin for 10 s.
Keep the sample on ice until loading (maximum 20 µL per well).

steps.title: Assemble electrophoresis chamber
steps.instruction: Set up the gel apparatus and add running buffer.

substeps.instruction: Remove the comb after the concentrating gel has polymerized.
Place the gel assembly into the electrophoresis chamber.
Prepare 1X running buffer from the 5X stock (0.125 M Tris, 0.96 M Glycine, 0.1 % SDS, pH 8.3) and fill the chamber between the glass plates up to the indicated fill line.

steps.title: Load samples and ladder
steps.instruction: Introduce protein standards and samples into the gel wells.

substeps.instruction: Load 3 µL of pre‑stained protein ladder into the first well.
Load up to 20 µL of each prepared sample into subsequent wells (each biological replicate in triplicate).

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Electrophorese the gel under the specified conditions.

substeps.instruction: Connect the chamber to power supply and run at 120 V for 90 min.

steps.title: Stain gel with Coomassie
steps.instruction: Visualize proteins by staining and destaining.

substeps.instruction: Prepare staining solution: 1 g L⁻¹ Brilliant Coomassie Blue, 10 % acetic acid, 40 % methanol.
Incubate the gel in staining solution for 30 min on a rocker shaker.
Wash the gel with distilled water to remove excess dye.
Destain in 10 % acetic acid / 40 % methanol solution overnight.
Wash the gel again with abundant water and photograph the result.

description: •Finally, the validation phase (Table 1), is detailed below from washing the samples to running the SDS-Page gel. As a next step it is expected to perform Western Blot of S. salar embryo chorion proteins to identify the specific proteins, not only at the 280 ATU stage, but at various stages of development (e.g. before activation/hydration/fertilization of the oocytes, after fertilization and/or at hatching).
